Aldwell and Schachter: Harmony and Voice Leading

Modulation examples from chapter 27, with Roman numerals under the notes

Seven modulation examples from chapter 27 of Aldwell, Schachter and Cadwallader’s Harmony and Voice Leading: Bach chorales, a Mozart trio and a short progression, with the Roman-numeral analysis under the notes (When in Rome). Play each one.

Seven examples from chapter 27 of Edward Aldwell, Carl Schachter and Allen Cadwallader’s Harmony and Voice Leading: four Bach chorales, a short progression from C minor to A♭ major in two versions, and an excerpt from Mozart’s Trio for Clarinet, Viola and Piano, K. 498.

How to read the labels and use the scores: Analysed Scores. For modulation itself, see Chapter 22.

Chapter 27

27-2a. Bach, Chorale 222

27-2b. Bach, Chorale 209

27-2c. Bach, Chorale 137

27-3. Bach, Chorale 207

27-4a. C minor to A♭ major

27-4b. C minor to A♭ major

27-7. Mozart, Trio for Clarinet, Viola, and Piano, K. 498

NoteFor teachers
  • Source: the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset’s encodings of the book’s examples (Néstor Nápoles López and others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs reads the MusicXML (src/aldwell), and every note was checked against music21’s reading of the same files.
  • Copyright: the book is in copyright. The chorales and the Mozart are public domain; 27-4a and 27-4b are the authors’ own progressions, a few bars each, as encoded in the dataset.
  • Not edited: the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.

For students

Aldwell, Edward, Carl Schachter, and Allen Cadwallader. Harmony and Voice Leading. Chapter 27, the source of the examples on the Aldwell and Schachter page. The dataset names the three authors but not the edition, which has not been checked.

Gotham, Mark, et al. When in Rome: A Meta-Corpus of Functional Harmony. GitHub. github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome. The analyses on this page (RomanText files), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Hutchinson, Robert. “Modulation.” Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom, ch. 22, U of Puget Sound. musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/Modulation.html. Tonicization against modulation, closely related keys, diatonic and chromatic pivot chords, and direct, common-tone and sequential modulation.

For teachers

Nápoles López, Néstor, et al. Key Modulation Dataset. GitHub (DDMAL). github.com/DDMAL/key_modulation_dataset. The encodings and analyses of the textbook examples, translated to RomanText by Nápoles López and copied into When in Rome.
